Justice for Ukraine (sponsored by Babel.ua)

By: Floris Kotze | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Why Justice Is Crucial and How We Tackle Its Challenges (really hard)

Unique Selling Point:
We received an invite to visit a country, finding its-self in the middle of a war being forgotten.
We take seek stories from Ukrainians, on the ground - seeking justice.
We hear from experts about their mission: to highlight
the ongoing efforts and challenges of
achieving justice for Ukraine.

Summary:
We will aim to travel outside the main city of Kyiv to get to speak to individuals affected by the war. Discussions with locals about their
experiences during the occupation. Discussing war crimes with researchers
who documented the Russian offences.

Further information:
Andriy Kostin
Discussing how the Prosecutor's Office investigates Russian war crimes.

Andriy Kostin

Script:


Opening Shots - Warsaw, Trains

Opening Link:
After 18 hours we've arrived in Warsaw Poland and after another day we should be at a border town ready to cross into Ukraine. We're going there when Ukraine is fighting off the back foot and we've been told them this will be toughest part of our journey.

VO:
It’s a gruelling journey made necessary by Ukraine’s ongoing war with Russia. It’s been two years since Moscow’s invasion and, as conflict rages in the East of the country, martial law has grounded all air traffic. But the long train journey to Kyiv was just the first of many challenges…

War Montage

Kyiv Link
This is Kyiv, the capital city of Ukraine, for centuries surrounding nations have fought wars to control it and it seems like that hasn't changed. As the Russian invasion intensifies another fight is emerging but it's not a battle being for guns and said with international law.

VO
With an end to the conflict nowhere in sight, Ukraine has none-the-less launched a campaign for justice.
(PAUSE) To understand what that means, we’re visiting the small towns and villages that stood in the way of the Russian advance on Kyiv two years ago… talking to the people still haunted by the brutality of the conflict.

Our journey will eventually take us to Bucha, a town that came to define this war; made famous by allegations of war crimes.

Raisa Kostenko
Do you know how many people
have died here? A child was brought here to the grandparents, and it was split in half!
Probably from the explosion...

VO:
Raisa Kostenko lost it all — her house reduced to rubble by artillery shelling.

Mykola Savchuk
They shot seventeen young guys here. They raped women here.

VO:
Mykola Savchuk was taken prisoner, allegedly tortured and beaten whilst in the prisoner camps. He was released as part of a prisoner exchange program.



Yuliia Baish
They tortured them, they also cut off the forehead of one boy.

VO
Yuliia Baish's husband, Vitali, was captured, killed, and buried in an unmarked grave. She found his body more than a year after Russia withdrew from the region.

Oleksndr
It was terrible for me because I knew a lot of people from this mass graves. The father of my friend was in this mass grave. My child mate was in this mass grave.

VO
March 2022, St. Andrew's Church in Bucha became a monument to war's horrors. After Russian forces withdrew, a MASS GRAVE was uncovered, revealing dozens of bodies.

Babies, teenagers, and the elderly showed signs of execution, their hands bound and faces scarred.This grim discovery in a previously peaceful town provided evidence of Russian war crimes committed on Ukrainian soil.

Oleksandr Ostapa, a lifelong resident and founder of TheBuchaCity, an online publication, is among those gathering evidence of war crimes. He hands what he finds to the authorities to help identify THOSE responsible for the killings.

Oleksndr
We have photos, we have videos, we have evidence from people from after the occupation.
We share this information with the police with international organisations. Just to help them to gather all evidence of war crimes in Bucha.

Prosecutor Andriy Kostin
We were all shocked. Practically all law enforcement system was allocated to there to document this atrocities to find out to identify the perpetrator(S).

VO:
As Ukraine’s Prosecutor General, Andriy Kostin is leading the efforts to bring Russian war criminals to justice.

UPS

Prosecutor Andriy Kostin
Most of the evidence we collected where from from the people we also uh collect the evidences for instance from the CCTV cameras uh state operational during the occupation.



VO:
Among the evidence is THIS clip of Russian soldiers capturing what Ukrainian authorities say - were civilians stationed at a Ukrainian checkpoint. (GAP) After the retreat, their bodies were found near a former Russian base in Bucha.

Prosecutor Andriy Kostin
Crimes committed by Russian war criminals - they are not incidental, they are a system, of and pattern of their conduct. They even didn't hide their atrocities, // practically uh the same types of crimes were committedKharkiv, given then later on when we liberated Kherson, in November 2022 - the same types of crime.

LINK
We just 20 km outside the capital city and all along this video up buildings that have been destroyed by Russian promise let us shows that people is always within which and the Threat is very real.

Shelter Scene
Govan
It's probably up here, I heard someone… we don't know where it is… Good morning.
“Morning…”
We're in the bomb shelter…
Govan
They say that Russians launched cruise missiles and several group of drones….
Journo
One is rocket is going to Aviev…. And one that is in the Kyiv region… and there is a question, are you in the shelter?
Govan
They are clearly concerned.

Govan
Sun is rising

VO
Almost two hours later - we get a message…

GAP

VO
Later that day, we hear that a Russian drone hit a fuel depot near Kyiv, affecting electricity supply. But, elsewhere in the country, the war’s impacts are far worse.

Daria Herasymchuk
Unfortunately the Russians do not stop their crimes. They continue to commit
every possible crime every day, including murder, violence and so on. Including, of course,
the deportation of Ukrainian children.

VO
Daria Herasymchuk is the advisor on children's rights to Ukraine's president, Vladimir Zelinsky. She claims the Russians are kidnapping Ukrainian children in regions they occupy and sending them across the border.

GAP

It’s difficult to verify but the International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Russian President, Vladimir Putin, last year.

AL Jazera Clip
- for alleged war crimes of deportation of children of Ukrainian occupied territories into the Russian Federation children….

Daria Herasymchuk
Two, three hundred thousand children. That's how many children could be there and the Russians could have potentially kidnapped. The children we brought back
is about twenty thousand children. We have their personal data. But it's a very, very
small part of what was of those actually kidnapped.
This is definitely genocide. And we will do our best… We don't know how many years it will take, but we will prove that it was genocide and they should be held responsible for it.

VO:
It’s amid this turmoil that Kostin is determined to ensure justice.

Prosecutor Andriy Kostin
At moment we have registered more than 129,000 incidents of all crimes.
And we have already 116 Russian war criminals convicted by Ukrainian courts.

Govan
Seeking a special tribunal the crimes of aggression
Prosecutor Andriy Kostin
We are trying to engage international community to establish a special trade you know, to prosecute the highest military and political leadership of Russian Federation. we expect these from Putin and maybe 20 to 30 people from the highest military political leadership who organised initiated and committed invasion of Russian Federation into Ukraine.

Prosecutor Andriy Kostin
If aggression is not committed there is no possibility to commit other war crimes.

VO:
The tribunal intends prosecuting Putin and members of his war cabinet in absentia. In other words none of those accused of war-time atrocities need to be present in the hearings.


VO
In the past weeks, Russia has offered ceasefire terms that many say are aimed at breaking Ukraine spirit. As most of Europe and the United States continue to rally behind Kyiv, unease is growing around threats by Vladimir Putin to resort to nuclear weapons. Whether he’s prepared to act on those threats is hard to know but, for Ukraine, continuing the fight is a matter of survival… and the hope that justice will come for the innocent victims of this war.

Govan Seeking a special tribunal the crimes of aggression Prosecutor Andriy Kostin We are trying to engage international community to establish a special trade you know, to prosecute the highest military and political leadership of Russian Federation. we expect these from Putin and maybe 20 to 30 people from the highest military political leadership who organised initiated and committed invasion of Russian Federation into Ukraine. Prosecutor Andriy Kostin If aggression is not committed there is no possibility to commit other war crimes. VO: The tribunal intends prosecuting Putin and members of his war cabinet in absentia. In other words none of those accused of war-time atrocities need to be present in the hearings. VO In the past weeks, Russia has offered ceasefire terms that many say are aimed at breaking Ukraine spirit. As most of Europe and the United States continue to rally behind Kyiv, unease is growing around threats by Vladimir Putin to resort to nuclear weapons. Whether he’s prepared to act on those threats is hard to know but, for Ukraine, continuing the fight is a matter of survival… and the hope that justice will come for the innocent victims of this war.
